notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: AbstractChannelHandlerContext.isNotValidPromise rejects promise.channel()!=channel()
notApplicableMethods.reason: CLR outbound methods accept EndPoint/message/CancellationToken and return consumer Tasks. Callers cannot submit a mutable producer belonging to another channel; that invalid input is absent from the public API.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: isNotValidPromise rejects VoidChannelPromise for close
notApplicableMethods.reason: The CLR API has no VoidChannelPromise argument or void producer object. CloseAsync always returns a normal observable Task; manufacturing this input would add the JVM facade the port deliberately avoids.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: isNotValidPromise rejects AbstractChannel.CloseFuture supplied as an operation promise
notApplicableMethods.reason: CloseCompletion is a consumer-only Task with no public setter, and CloseAsync has no completion-producer parameter. A close-notification Task cannot be supplied as a mutable close-operation producer.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: validateWrite releases referenceCounted when a wrong-channel promise argument is rejected before transport ownership
notApplicableMethods.reason: The sole rejection trigger in this original helper is channel2.newPromise() supplied to channel1.write. No such parameter exists in CLR WriteAsync. Its exact validation/reference-release scenario is inapplicable, not replaced by an unrelated handler-throw test. Existing native cancellation and rejected-dispatch tests separately cover supported input ownership.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: validateWrite releases referenceCounted when wrong-channel promise is supplied to writeAndFlush
notApplicableMethods.reason: WriteAndFlushAsync likewise accepts no completion producer, so a foreign-channel promise cannot enter validation. Do not pretend a generic write failure is the original scenario; supported cancellation/rejection ownership remains separately tested.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: ensurePromiseUseCorrectExecutor cascades a context-owned DefaultChannelPromise into a caller-supplied foreign-executor promise; six attached listeners observe context ownership
notApplicableMethods.reason: Native Tasks expose no executor-bearing mutable promise input and do not automatically schedule callbacks on a channel. This exact cascade is absent. A separately counted native test completes all six operations from a foreign producer and explicitly regains the handler owner before observing state; it is a CLR alternative, not the original assertion ported unchanged.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: VoidChannelPromise.tryFailure routes a write failure to ExceptionCaught without a returned completion future
notApplicableMethods.reason: Every CLR write returns an observable Task, so there is no explicit VoidChannelPromise failure-notification mode. The native alternative awaits that Task and preserves the original exception identity; it does not manually fire ExceptionCaught to simulate the absent API.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Registration listener initializes OioSocketChannel on a dedicated OioEventLoopGroup
notApplicableMethods.reason: CLR Transport has one asynchronous System.Net.Sockets TcpSocketChannel, not a separate obsolete JVM blocking OIO channel/event-loop family. The mapped NIO registration test executes the same portable listener contract on the actual CLR TCP implementation. Running that identical CLR case twice would not port an OIO backend.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Register a caller-supplied channel-associated Java ChannelPromise after loop shutdown. Its monitor/future completes with RejectedExecutionException and its channel closes, but assertFalse(latch.await(1 second)) requires that the already-attached listener never runs because dispatch through the stopped channel executor is rejected. notApplicableMethods.reason: Native RegisterAsync returns a Task and has no mutable caller-supplied Java promise input. Task consumers can observe a fault through the CLR scheduler even after the event loop stops. Faking a promise/listener executor or silently changing the one-second non-notification assertion would change the source contract. Review the whole original method separately without a mapped count or xUnit skip; the positive native consumer/closure counterpart is supplementary. Java executes the unchanged original, including its one-second negative listener observation.

clrDecisions.subject: Windows UDP truncation
clrDecisions.decision: ReceiveFromAsync does not publish the sender endpoint on WSAEMSGSIZE. This bounds staging per outstanding Windows receive but adds a copy; no platform-performance parity claim.

clrDecisions.decision: Native Task.WhenAll covers currently implemented aggregate operations. Per-channel result/failure inspection remains open; it is not silently excluded as JVM-only.

clrDecisions.subject: Output gathering and cancellation
clrDecisions.decision: Borrowed ReadOnlyMemory arrays and ReadOnlySequence segments replace NIO buffers. Cancellation atomically claims an unflushed Task but retains an empty queue entry until flush; every entry is made consistent before cancelled messages are released or writability callbacks run. TCP sends composite segments; UDP copies segmented content into a single pooled borrow to preserve datagram boundaries.

clrDecisions.subject: Late native I/O completion
clrDecisions.decision: Unlike selector readiness, a CLR receive/accept may already have consumed input when AutoRead or registration is revoked. Keep at most one completed native input operation per channel and dispatch it only after read/registration admission; a close wakes the waiter and releases borrowed memory or the accepted socket. Resume and callback ownership follow the currently registered worker. The source default receive-message limit is 16 for TCP, UDP and server channels; LocalChannel remains 1.

clrDecisions.subject: Pending write producers
clrDecisions.decision: Use native TaskCompletionSource for producer identity/Remove ownership and Task for consumers, Task.WhenAll for aggregation, and CancellationToken for queue/transport cancellation. Queue cancellation retains message ownership until removal and stops at transport flush. Producers are completed on the assigned executor when asynchronous writes finish; Task continuations themselves still require caller-selected dispatch. No Future/Promise/voidPromise facade or JVM Recycler is introduced. The original accounting estimate remains configurable and is not a CLR object-size claim. All source listener reentrance scenarios use default TCS producers and ExecuteSynchronously continuations; consumers await the native bridge when required.

clrDecisions.subject: Coalescing queue completions
clrDecisions.decision: BCL LinkedList stores buffers and native TaskCompletionSource/Action<Task> metadata; no DelegatingChannelPromiseNotifier or Future/Promise/voidPromise facade. Source initial capacity is only a sizing hint, which LinkedList does not use. AddFirst without a producer represents void completion. ReleaseAndFailAll uses Task.FromException and is inherited by CoalescingBufferQueue. WriteAndRemoveAllAsync drains synchronously then exposes native asynchronous write completion with Task.WhenAll. Bridges dispatch notifications to the assigned executor; rejected dispatch fails the native producer and returned Task instead of leaving it pending. Aggregate continuations use ExecuteSynchronously for original inline reentrance; callers selecting asynchronous TCS continuations must await their work. CopyTo intentionally keeps the source shallow-copy ownership contract.

clrDecisions.subject: Native channel pools
clrDecisions.decision: AcquireAsync returns Task<IChannel> and uses CancellationToken; the pool keeps its native TCS producer private. Cancelled consumers still trigger release when pending connect/health checks finish. Async health is Func<IChannel,Task<bool>>, with health invocation and all pool notifications on the channel event loop. BCL LinkedList under a short storage lock replaces a concurrent deque; no user callback runs under that lock. ConcurrentDictionary insertion closes discarded pools outside map operations. Native CloseAsync/DisposeAsync replace GlobalEventExecutor blocking bridges; synchronous Close retains the source blocking caller contract. SimpleChannelPool Close drains available channels and intentionally does not become a permanently closed pool. Bootstrap.Clone(IEventLoop) supplies the source explicit registration owner without making native IEventLoop a fake IEventLoopGroup. JVM stacktrace suppression and mutable Promise overloads are not reproduced.

clrDecisions.subject: Fixed pool ownership and deadlines
clrDecisions.decision: Use a private native TCS per acquisition, CancellationToken for consumer cancellation, TimeSpan for configured durations, a BCL linked pending queue, and ScheduleAsync with a cancellation source per deadline. All count/queue mutations run on one configured event executor. Inner base acquisition remains uncancelled so a cancelled consumer still returns a later successful channel. Base results are explicitly queued back to the pool executor, supplying bounded completion depth when many cancelled requests drain. Handler exceptions return a slot, but ChannelNotAcquiredFromPoolException does not. Native async close replaces the source GlobalEventExecutor blocking bridge and keeps map Get/Remove nonblocking across workers. Monotonic executor ticker and unchecked deadline subtraction preserve wrap-safe expiry; duration conversion saturates rather than overflows. JVM fillInStackTrace suppression is omitted while preserving its comment and native stacks.

clrDecisions.subject: Local segmented reads and original read budgets
clrDecisions.decision: Use the existing indexed ByteBuf.WriteBytes overload for coalescing, exactly as upstream: a live CLR ReadOnlyMemory can describe only contiguous storage, so treating every ByteBuf as one memory is invalid. Indexed transfer supports every segment and preserves source reader indices. Restore the source nonempty-inbound condition before consuming a pending read, so a late empty peer notification cannot lose the next manual Read. Original concurrency/read count inputs and 5-second deadlines stay unchanged; native async test signals replace blocking latches and Task continuations explicitly regain executor ownership before Read. The package-visible inbound queue is exposed to the original friend-assembly test by an internal read-only empty-state property, without exposing a mutable public collection.

clrDecisions.subject: Local lifecycle, native connect completion and close-owned writes
clrDecisions.decision: Keep native Task/TCS producers, consumer cancellation and explicit owner dispatch. Complete the on-owner connect operation before ChannelActive while retaining asynchronous continuation scheduling. SocketException(ConnectionRefused) represents failed remote acceptance and IOException represents own/closed-channel failure. Never touch a pending accepted peer owned by a server or registration loop. Finish peer reads using the source writeInProgress ordering. A short CLR inbound acceptance gate joins publication with close/seal, with no user retain/release callbacks under it. Preserve original write/close test assertions; use deterministic CLR supplements for inline write finalization reentrance and retained-reference handoff races. CLR pending-connect cancellation cancels the private producer and closes on its owner; later server acceptance cannot reactivate the client. A delayed separate-executor initializer must still receive Registered/read/removal after close; pending-context admission happens before executor dispatch and invocation-state filtering after it. Source volatile link/state visibility is retained.

clrDecisions.subject: Pipeline mutations and optional concurrent removal
clrDecisions.decision: Port the three original lookup forms using C# string, IChannelHandler and Type. A shared TryRemoveContext atomically unlinks under the existing pipeline gate, defers removal until first registration or queues it on the assigned owner, and returns false for a lost unlink race. Optional removal returns null; normal removal throws KeyNotFoundException. Preserve buffered forwarding through removed/replaced contexts and unresolved source write completions. Native Task/TCS and BCL queue/channel helpers retain the original callback counts and executor order without reproducing a Java Promise API.

clrDecisions.subject: Pipeline pending admission and primary initialization failure
clrDecisions.decision: Use the existing IOrderedEventExecutor marker and private CLR volatile/Interlocked state to preserve source ADD_PENDING admission without recreating Java field-updater APIs. An unordered executor can deliver an event before queued HandlerAdded starts; a normal event loop cannot. Added state is committed before reentrant user callbacks, and removal is finalized even if a callback throws. Added-failure cleanup logs secondary removal errors while preserving the primary pipeline exception. Pre-cancelled tokens replace supplied cancelled promises; native cancellation/dispatch Tasks are explicitly observed before inspecting completion and buffer ownership. Recheck admission when routing a callback failure because that callback may already have removed its own context. The original DefaultEventLoop-based alternating helper retains the existing native ordered marker.

clrDecisions.subject: Pipeline mask, method-level decisions and native completion roles
clrDecisions.decision: Preserve meaningful @Skip behavior using a non-inherited CLR method attribute, concrete interface-map targets and an immutable weak-key cache. Skip event-specific forwarding only on the same executor; crossing a foreign executor remains necessary for order. Do not reintroduce caller-owned Java promises, void promises, mutable close futures or a duplicate blocking OIO backend merely to compile invalid-input tests. Explicitly reviewed unsupported source methods remain separate from mapped source cases and native supplements. Task consumers must explicitly dispatch owner state access; their returned failure Task preserves exception identity.

clrDecisions.subject: Combined handler contexts and native completion plumbing
clrDecisions.decision: Keep ChannelHandlerContext as the existing concrete public type and permit internal delegation by virtualizing IsRemoved and its forwarding operations. Both owned contexts delegate to the current outer context and expose the outer Handler identity exactly as source; removal flags and callbacks remain independent. Returned Tasks preserve the positive completion intent of testPromisesPassed, while source-specific invalid mutable-input tests remain distinct. Six additional native tests verify facade identity, live neighbors, foreign-thread removal, lifecycle failure/finally, removal failure and controlled Task outcomes.

clrDecisions.subject: Datagram multicast TTL option
clrDecisions.decision: DefaultDatagramChannelConfig.getTimeToLive/setTimeToLive and the NIO IP_MULTICAST_TTL option concern multicast, not Socket.Ttl. Use SocketOptionName.MulticastTimeToLive at the socket family IP/IPv6 level with 0..255 validation. Two supplemental CLR cases independently read the actual socket option, preserve unicast TTL, round-trip 0/17/255 and reject -1/256/int.MaxValue. Both fail against the former unicast mapping. Multicast interface/address options and membership fixtures remain open.

clrDecisions.subject: UDP testsuite, multicast selection and connected lifecycle
clrDecisions.decision: Track selected testsuite originals separately from the exhaustive 274-file Transport inventory. Preserve both pooled/adaptive allocators, IPv4/IPv6 families, all buffer representations/wraps and original helper assertions. Config options reflect actual socket state. Track ASM memberships with BCL tuple keys to preserve repeated join/leave behavior. Source-specific membership/block and Windows-excluded IPv6 multicast packet fixtures remain open. Use the documented Winsock zero-address UDP connect to disconnect without replacing its bound socket; retain channel peer state separately from Socket cached connection state. Datagram individual write failures do not close a channel that may send to another peer; unresolved endpoints fail before native send and release ownership. Registered-only activity defers CLR receive until a first send implicitly binds the socket. The public DatagramChannelConfig disabled-loopback contract and DefaultDatagramChannelConfig behavior are retained using !Socket.MulticastLoopback. NioDatagramChannelConfig forwards IP_MULTICAST_LOOP directly despite that disabled-name contract; native tests independently verify actual kernel loopback state, not just getter/setter symmetry.

clrDecisions.subject: Source-specific multicast, read failures and resolver cancellation
clrDecisions.decision: IPv4 source inclusion/drop and all-source blocking use BCL SocketOptionName with platform-reviewed IP_MREQ_SOURCE byte layout (Windows group/source/interface; Linux group/interface/source). Tuple keys distinguish source memberships, reject ASM/SSM mixing and retain idempotence. Blocking a missing membership is a no-op; implicit block uses the selected native multicast interface consistently with implicit join instead of the original bound-wildcard lookup pitfall. IPv6 source filtering and other-platform ABI remain unimplemented and explicit. Socket read failures emit ReadComplete then ExceptionCaught and preserve outstanding manual read permission; other read errors close. Connect cancellation races an independent resolver Task and closes promptly even if the resolver ignores its token; observe late failures without changing the canceled result or retaining the channel.

clrDecisions.subject: Initializer extension discovery and ordered typed bootstrap state
clrDecisions.decision: Use explicit scoped process-wide Register rather than inventing a Java SPI/Classpath loader in CLR. Default registry is empty; opt-in/log-only mode, source floating-point priority order, immutable captures and exception isolation preserve actual policy. Client/listener callbacks run during pre-registration initialization; child callback runs after child options/attributes/handler setup and before registration. Notifications retain source role/thread-local semantics. OrderedDictionary preserves option insertion order; typed-key dictionaries retain attribute values/actions, replace updates and remove nulls without materializing an empty channel attribute. Both client and server clone/capture state independently. Preserve Java LinkedHashMap plus synchronized snapshots using OrderedDictionary guarded by a private lock, and ConcurrentHashMap attributes using ConcurrentDictionary of typed keys/value-application pairs. Caller mutation cannot corrupt option snapshots; clone option order remains independent. Other builder-wide concurrency remains unreviewed.

clrDecisions.subject: Bootstrap configuration views and failure/completion representation
clrDecisions.decision: Use native get-only live Config views and independent ReadOnlyDictionary snapshots backed by ordered BCL maps. Remove Java self-typed generic bootstrap plumbing; resolver metadata is object identity while actual resolution remains typed, atomically paired in an immutable record. Null resolver resets the default. Retain source volatile visibility. Task consumers explicitly return to the event loop for owner callbacks; Tasks do not inherit Java ChannelFuture listener affinity. The original factory-failure method requires a dummy FailedChannel result carrier, so it is reviewed as CLR-inapplicable in full and has a separately counted native Task-fault alternative. Preserve its completion deadline and exception identity without fabricating a channel.

clrDecisions.subject: TCP direction shutdown, allocator-owned manual read batches and final input-read notification
clrDecisions.decision: Use Task-based direction shutdown, output before input, always attempt both and preserve the original output exception via ExceptionDispatchInfo. IOException replaces closed-channel representation; the dedicated ChannelOutputShutdownException subtype preserves queued-write failure meaning. Output shutdown fails/releases queued ownership and emits its event even when the native call fails, retaining input registration and communication. One explicit Read admits the whole allocator-approved available batch; a held first native completion still respects disabled AutoRead and deregistration. CLR has no later readiness callback after EOF, so the next admitted logical read emits the final ReadComplete/InputShutdownReadComplete pair once on the current owner. Source tests keep original data sizes, allocator budgets, boolean combinations, direction roles, ownership and deadlines. No selector, Java future facade or copied comment archive is introduced.

clrDecisions.subject: TCP write-error classification and half-close backend/platform conditions
clrDecisions.decision: Java SocketException inherits IOException; CLR SocketException does not. Treat both as I/O errors for AutoClose=true; otherwise shut output only, wrap the original cause, release queued references and keep input usable. Close transport before faulting flushed tasks; keep separate unflushed closed causes. SO_LINGER=0 must skip orderly Socket.Shutdown so Dispose sends an abortive reset. Preserve the original Windows assumption instead of forcing Unix reset/read ordering onto Windows. The kernel-specific no-manual-read half-close scenario is explicitly excluded just as the original excludes NIO/OIO; the CLR backend counterpart requests reads and stays supplementary. Preserve the original incorrect Context-cast scenario as its actual exception/peer-close path and separately test a real half-close. All eight SocketHalfClosed declarations are accounted without rewriting assertions or counting gated/no-op wrapper calls as passed test bodies.

clrDecisions.subject: Event-loop native scheduling, registration result roles and polymorphic queue metrics
clrDecisions.decision: Java virtual instance dispatch must remain virtual in CLR: replace the hidden new PendingTasks member by a true override, with a source-shaped held-owner test proving ordinary plus tail counts through the parent type. Native Task/CTS retain scheduling deadlines, non-overlap and cancellation while avoiding Java scheduled futures/promises. DelayNanos expects the source absolute clock input, so native helper adds the ticker initial offset to elapsed nanoseconds before conversion. A caller-supplied channel promise that completes but cannot dispatch its listener through a stopped owner has no native producer-input equivalent; it stays explicitly CLR-inapplicable, while native Task consumer notification is separately verified. Four deregistration enum forms fold to the two native context/channel routes; owner dispatch is explicit before and after moving the real channel. Original comments/assertions/timing bounds, tail removal/drain and cleanup count remain intact.

clrDecisions.subject: Native I/O registration, server accept batching and wakeup semantics
clrDecisions.decision: Track actual owned channel registrations in the production CLR loop, expose owner-only read-only snapshots and feed registration counts into suspension admission. Register/deregister/migrate/close/forced-failure paths maintain membership. A BCL listening Socket is owned directly by native listener/stream constructors. Reuse the existing source server allocator (message count, ignore bytes) rather than the stream adaptive allocator; collect an available accept batch before callbacks, deliver partial accepts before completion/error, preserve manual read permission on empty recoverable failures and consume it when messages were delivered. IOException/CLR SocketException are recoverable, other accept failures close; yield after synchronous failures. Java selector rebuilding/identity/interest masks and NioChannelOption adapter roles are explicitly excluded in full, not represented by dummy CLR types. Source B/C loop helpers now use AutoResetEvent to wake a wait: Thread.Interrupt is not a safe CLR translation of Java wakeup, because CLR can interrupt Monitor lock acquisition during callback logging. Real source timing/ownership assertions remain unchanged. Completed native write operations release their temporary borrow before publishing a queued failure, matching source release-before-notification while retaining any still-running native operation borrow during close.

clrDecisions.subject: Unix domain stream and listener channels
clrDecisions.decision: Share native asynchronous read, write, connect and accept behavior with TCP. Use BCL AF_UNIX endpoints and sockets, preserve role-specific receive/send/backlog/half-close options and let BCL socket disposal clean up paths it bound. Capability checks replace the JDK version gate. The JDK unsupported-option and three VoidPromise identity fixtures are reviewed as complete methods. A test-only wakeup signal is serialized with disposal to keep the original event-loop assertions runnable.
